definitions.explanation: the sector of the economy that provides services rather than manufactured goods

examples.japanese: サービス{業|ぎょう}で{働|はたら}いている。
examples.english: I work in the service industry.

examples.japanese: サービス{業|ぎょう}は{休日|きゅうじつ}が{不規則|ふきそく}になりがちだ。
examples.english: In the service industry, days off tend to be irregular.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{経済|けいざい}はサービス{業|ぎょう}を{中心|ちゅうしん}に{成長|せいちょう}してきた。
examples.english: Japan's economy has grown centering on the service industry.

notes:
Composed of サービス (service) + {業|ぎょう} (industry, business). Covers a wide range of businesses including hospitality, retail, food service, healthcare, and entertainment.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- サービス{業|ぎょう}に{従事|じゅうじ}する: to be engaged in the service industry
- サービス{業|ぎょう}で{働|はたら}く: to work in the service industry
- サービス{業|ぎょう}の{人手不足|ひとでぶそく}: labor shortage in the service sector
- サービス{業|ぎょう}{全般|ぜんぱん}: service industry as a whole

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {接客業|せっきゃくぎょう}: customer-facing work — specifically jobs involving direct interaction with customers
- {製造業|せいぞうぎょう}: manufacturing industry — produces physical goods, in contrast to services
- {第三次産業|だいさんじさんぎょう}: tertiary industry — the economic classification that includes services

NOTE: In Japan, サービス{業|ぎょう} workers often work weekends and holidays since those are peak customer times. This is a common topic in discussions about work-life balance.
